messages.author: 5edd60dd3319aa0e
messages.subject: Vanishing line segments
parts:
Hi All,

I'm doing a dot-plot with line segments drawn to each dot. It looks
fine until I change the axis limits, then the line segments vanish.
The program and a small bit of the data is below. This was in 2.10.1
so I just downloaded 2.11.1 and the latest ggplot2. It shows the same
result. Any ideas?

Thanks,
Bob

P.S. the machine runs Windows 7 64


# PageRank Plot of Stat Software Web Sites 6/19/2010

statpkgs <- read.csv( stdin(), header=TRUE )
Software, Site, PageRank
R, www.r-project.org, 8
Revolution, www.revolutionanalytics.com/, 3
XL-Solutions, www.xlsolutions-corp.com/, 5

#End of data
statpkgs
statpkgs$Software <- reorder( statpkgs$Software, statpkgs$PageRank )

attach(statpkgs)

# This plot is good but I want the scale to go from 1 to 10:

library("ggplot2")

ggplot(statpkgs, aes(Software, PageRank) ) +
geom_point(size=4) +
geom_segment( aes(Software, PageRank, xend=Software, yend=0) ) +
scale_x_discrete("Analytical Software") +
scale_y_continuous("Google PageRank of Web Site" ) +
coord_flip()

# Here I set the scale but the geom_segments disappear

ggplot(statpkgs, aes(Software, PageRank) ) +
geom_point(size=4) +
geom_segment( aes(Software, PageRank, xend=Software, yend=0) ) +
scale_x_discrete("Analytical Software") +
scale_y_continuous("Google PageRank of Web Site") +
scale_y_continuous( limits = c(1,10) ) +
coord_flip()

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: Vanishing line segments
parts:
Hi Bob,

It's because the start of the line is outside the range of the plot. I
think you want the y limits to be c(0, 10).

Hadley

Bob

messages.author: ec7010d530c9f38f
messages.subject: Re: Vanishing line segments
parts:
Hi there,

I am experiencing the same issue. When you use

>geom_segments(x=a,y=b,xend=c,yend=d)

and specify a scale limit on the x-axis

>scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,10))

then only segments that are included are those where x and xend (so start and end) fall into the range of the scale (0,10). Is there a possibility where you can include segments where the x (so the start of the segment) does not fall in the range of the scale but xend does?

Many thanks in advance,

Irsan

parts:

>
> I am experiencing the same issue. When you use
>
> >geom_segments(x=a,y=b,xend=c,yend=d)
>
> and specify a scale limit on the x-axis
>
> >scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,10))
>
> then only segments that are included are those where x and xend (so start and end) fall into the range of the scale (0,10). Is there a possibility where you can include segments where the x (so the start of the segment) does not fall in the range of the scale but xend does?

scale_x_continuous excludes all data outside of the limits and plots what remains. Use the xlim argument of coord_cartesian instead to just physically zoom on a region of interest.

Jean-Olivier Irisson

According to the NEWS file, there's supposed to be another alternative:

* The new `oob` (out of bounds) parameter controls how scales deals with
values outside the limits. The default action is `censor` - see `clip`
for another option.

but I haven't been able to figure out how to use it:

ggplot(d,aes(x,y))+geom_line()+scale_x_continuous(lim=c(1,10),oob=clip)

doesn't work, and I can't find any other documentation anywhere.

Ben Bolker

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Vanishing line segments
parts:
There was a bug where the oob argument wasn't being used, but it should be fixed now in the development version:
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/383

It works with oob=squish, but I don't think it works with oob=clip. I believe the valid methods are listed here:
https://github.com/hadley/scales/blob/master/R/bounds.r

-Winston
